analysis: The code calls `name.substring(lastIndexOfDot + 1)` only when `lastIndexOfDot >= 0`, which means there is at least one dot in `name`. At that point, `lastIndexOfDot` is a valid index within `name`, so `lastIndexOfDot + 1` is at least 1 and at most `name.length()` (since `lastIndexOfDot` is at most `name.length()-1`). The documentation states that `IndexOutOfBoundsException` is thrown if `beginIndex` is negative or larger than the length of the string. Here, `beginIndex` is non-negative and cannot exceed the length (it can equal the length, which is allowed), so the exception condition is avoided. The only declared exception is `IndexOutOfBoundsException`, and its throwing condition is fully prevented by the guard condition.
remark: The exception `IndexOutOfBoundsException` is not thrown because the guard `lastIndexOfDot >= 0` ensures that `beginIndex` is valid: it is always between 1 and `name.length()` inclusive. The only scenario that could cause the exception would be a negative `beginIndex` (impossible) or a `beginIndex` greater than the string length (impossible because `lastIndexOfDot` is always a valid index less than the length).
